thread:
marie: Heads-up, deployed v3.9.1 at 18:02 UTC. Immediately started seeing alert storms and some 5xxs reported by synthetic checks. I triggered a fast rollback but noticed key dashboards went blank. Anyone oncall able to triage?

deploy-bot: Deployment v3.9.1 -> rollback initiated by marie at 18:04 UTC. Canary traffic diverted. Logs: rollback-started.
:gear: request-id=abcd-1234

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-01. Paging @eng-oncall. Severity: P2 (partial customer impact).

tom: I'm on it. I got paged but haven't been able to see the normal route latency dashboard — looks like the 'routes.*' metrics are missing from the dashboard timeframe. Are metrics backfilled? :confused:

aj: saw the same. Grafana returns 404 for the dashboard slug `/dash/route-latency` for a bit then returns empty panels. Could be the dashboard folder reorganization in the deploy? I didn't touch dashboards in the deploy though.

sre-jen: taking lead. marie, timeline and exact svc names you rolled? I want the exact feature-flag toggles you flipped.

marie: rolled the traffic_split and flipped ff_new-routing:true (feature flag). We only changed routing prefix for canary (service name: routing-svc -> routing-svc-v2). Rollback flipped ff_new-routing:false at 18:04.

ops-liz: quick check: prometheus shows metrics for `routing_requests_total` are still being scraped but I see a parallel metric `routing_v2_requests_total` that started at deploy time. Dashboards were templated on the old metric name and didn't handle the v2 prefix. So panels went blank when canary started reporting v2 metrics.

marie: that explains blank panels. But why did alerts fire? The CPU/5xx alerting rules are referencing `sum(rate(routing_requests_total[1m]))` — if traffic moved to routing_v2_requests_total, rule evaluation drops to zero and then alerting thresholds are not hit? I would expect drop-to-zero to silence, not create noise.

aj: two things: 1) The alerting team has a muted-rule automation that *silences* alerts for specific rules during deploys, but that automation matched on dashboard tags which were removed by the dashboard reorg, so it didn't apply. 2) We have an alert that fires on missing metrics (evaluates to firing when absence > 60s) — it spiked because metric name change looked like a missing metric. That generated the noisy pages.

product-ryan: customers reported intermittent API errors though — the synthetic 5xxs were real for a subset of requests routed to v2. So there's real customer impact for some users, not just noise. We should treat as partial outage until rollback fully stabilized.

sre-jen: plan: 1) confirm rollback completed and no v2 traffic remains, 2) mute the missing-metric alert temporarily, 3) re-enable dashboard templating that handles both metric names, 4) postmortem and runbook update. Assigning steps.

marie: rollback status — deploy-bot logs say finished at 18:06 and traffic diverted back, but I can still see traces to routing-v2 in the traces UI (sampled). Investigating.

aj: muting alert rule `Alert: metric_missing` for the namespace for 1h now: `alertmanager silence add --match 'alertname=metric_missing, team=ingest' --duration=1h` (did via chatops). Should quiet pages while we stabilize.

ops-liz: running queries:
```
# check current series
curl -s 'http://prometheus/api/v1/series?match[]=routing_requests_total' | jq '. | length'
# inspect rule eval
kubectl logs deploy/prometheus-rule-evaluator -n monitoring --since=1h | tail -n 200
```

marie: found the remaining traffic — there was a small replica (1/3 of canary) still pegged on v2 due to a job that stuck the flag in the older cluster. Killing that job fixed it. I scaled that deployment down: `kubectl scale deploy routing-svc-v2 --replicas=0 -n prod`.

oncall-bot: Update: Incident INC-2026-0423-01 status -> Mitigated (partial). Pager suppression active.

tom: confirming RTT and 5xxs back to baseline for global synthetic checks. Logs show the 5xxs were a config path mismatch in v2 handler — we should capture that in the postmortem.

sre-jen: Good. Immediate mitigation done. Two quick followups for postmortem: 1) dashboard/alert ownership matrix must include deploy choreography changes (so automation that mutes alerts can match on deploy tags even if dashboards move). 2) Add a deploy-time canary-metric-compatibility check that fails the deploy if metrics emit with a different name prefix unless we've added shim rules. I'll file the postmortem and assign owners.

aj: also propose an alert rule change: change the missing-metric alert to require >5m absence for high-churn metrics or add a runbook label so it pages differently during deploy windows. Right now it trips in <1m which is too sensitive around rollouts.

product-ryan: can we add a quick customer-communication note? I can ping impacted accounts with what happened and what we did.

marie: thanks everyone. I clipped the traces and added a minimal repro to the ticket. Will include the exact CLI steps I used for rollback + the stuck job fix.

ops-liz: To-do list I captured:
- update silence automation to match deploy metadata (owner: aj)
- add backward-compatible metric shim or fail-safe in deploy (owner: ops-liz)
- relax metric-missing alert for templated dashboards (owner: sre-jen)
- postmortem doc + timeline (owner: marie)

sre-jen: handing to followup oncall: @tom you'll own the postmortem draft and we will schedule RCA sync tomorrow. Thanks all. :heart:

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423-01 update: assigned to tom for followups.

marie: closing thread here, will link to postmortem when ready. :wave:
